body:
Review pass 13. Epic 4 is moving through kernel.R and task.R now, so I checked the one acceptance item that is a clean grep and stayed out of the rest.

DELIVERED, verified: "Hot-loop object-size counters are replaced by static owned-buffer planning". R/kernel.R and R/task.R now contain ZERO object.size / .measured_object_bytes calls - they previously sat in the innermost loop body - and task.R max_*_bytes fields are down from 17 to 2. That was one of the original review findings, so it is closed on the effect-form side.

NEW p2, bd-01KZXJ882H70KWBCHQ4HAZZN50: the same pattern survives in measurement-kernel.R, which is not in your Epic 4 reservation.

- measurement-kernel.R:332-339 has two object.size() calls inside the per-feature-block loop (:327), itself inside the per-partition loop (:325). Both quantities are known statically from the plan - relation_block is q x length(features) doubles, factor_slice is nrow(operator) x length(features).

- measurement-kernel.R:236-238 is the sharper one. matrix_bytes() sizes a buffer by ALLOCATING it: object.size(matrix(0, rows, columns)), called four times at :242-245. A memory preflight that allocates the buffers it is deciding whether it can afford is self-defeating. At q=200, feature_block=20000 that is 32 MB per call, ~128 MB across the four, before it reports whether the plan fits. Noted on Epic 8 too, since the 4 GiB peak-RSS gate would be measuring a preflight that inflates the number it gates on.

The replacement is exact arithmetic, verified across shapes: object.size(matrix(0,r,c)) == 8*r*c + 216 exactly at (12,50000), (200,20000) and (3,10).

- :239-241 also walks object.size over every measurement leg operator, i.e. the dense p-wide operators - the largest objects in that subsystem - for a diagnostic. Line 634 is in the benchmark harness and is fine.

Not urgent, no correctness impact. Filing so the measurement kernel does not quietly keep the pattern the effect-form kernel just shed, since that is the subsystem that has to reach brain scale.
